newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas mixed in continued volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas mixed in continued volatile trading.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly unchanged in Louisiana but higher in the Midcontinent and south Texas Wednesday, as cold temperatures continued to take their toll on supplies, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices slipped into the mid-$4.30s early after NYMEX opened lower, but then rebounded to $4.50 when reports surfaced that gas was scarce in the producing region.

Temperatures in the region, including southern Texas, were about 30 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal, which were about seven to eight degrees milder than originially expected. More seasonable temperatures are expected to arrive Sunday.
In south Texas, the market hovered mostly around $4.50, up more than five cents from Tuesday, as temperatures dipped below freezing.
In the market areas, New York city-gate prices ranged anywhere from $4.50 to $4.70, as compared with about $4.60 seen late Tuesday.
Appalachian prices were pressured by mild weather in the region, as traders reported closing deals in the $4.20s to about $4.50, down an average of 10 cents.

Severely cold temperatures in the mid-section of the U.S. resulted in some pipeline freeze-offs, traders said. This tightness in supply caused prices to jump into the $4.90s at Demarcation on Northern and into the $4.70s and $4.80s on most of the other Midcontinent pipelines.
These prices compare with Tuesday's average trading range of $4.60-4.65.
Temperatures in the region are expected to moderate this weekend but still remain below-normal through next week.

In west Texas, where supplies are moving eastward and into the Midcontinent markets, Permian gas prices fell an average of two cents to the high-$4.70s to low-$4.80s. Deals were reported done anywhere from the mid-$4.60s to about $5.

Expectations for milder air this weekend in the Southwest put downward pressure on prices at the southern California border. Deals were reported done in the $4.50s, down more than 10 cents from Tuesday.
Traders said they expected an average withdrawal between 67 and 72 billion cubic feet to appear in today's American Gas Association storage report.
